summary:
We developed ASTRAEA: Space Mission Simulator, an interactive, browser-based mission architecture and 3D orbital flight game. Players manage an end-to-end space mission across six connected phases—Concept Selection, 3D CAD Subsystem Assembly, Launch Vehicle Integration, 3D Orbital Flight Operations, Deep Space Network Science Downlink, and Post-Flight Engineering Review—across 12 solar-system destinations or custom missions.
It directly addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge by turning abstract engineering trade-offs into live, playable decisions. Every choice across structure, power (solar vs. MMRTG), propulsion, thermal control, telecom, and scientific payloads dynamically updates inverse-square solar flux, eclipse battery depth-of-discharge, wet mass, and grant budgets—and players fly the exact spacecraft they built in 3D orbit.
This is important because students rarely get to experiment with a full mission lifecycle. By making real aerospace systems engineering accessible in any web browser with zero installation, ASTRAEA builds practical STEM intuition for how competing constraints shape mission success.
details:
We created ASTRAEA: Space Mission Simulator, an interactive, browser-based space mission design game built for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. It lets students and participants design, manage, launch, pilot, and evaluate a complete space mission from initial concept to post-flight review while navigating real-world engineering trade-offs.

What it does & how it works:
Players progress through a coupled six-phase mission lifecycle:

  1. Concept: Select from 12 solar-system mission profiles (including Low Earth Orbit Climate Surveillance, Lunar Shackleton Crater Ice Survey, Mars Sample Return, Europa Astrobiology, Titan Cryo-Explorer, 16 Psyche, Asteroid Kinetic Deflection, and a Solar Corona Grazing Probe) or build a custom target mission. Players evaluate required
    inverse-square solar flux, radiation exposure, one-way communication latency, and grant budgets.
  2. CAD Bay: Assemble a 3D spacecraft across 8 coupled subsystems (Structure, Power, Battery, Propulsion, ADCS, Telecom, Thermal, and Payload) with an exploded-assembly inspection slider. Every component or propellant change dynamically recalculates wet mass, Tsiolkovsky
    power balance, eclipse battery Depth-of-Discharge, and thermal equilibrium.
  3. Launch: Match total spacecraft wet mass and escape requirements to a launch vehicle at LC-39A (SmallSat, Medium Lift, Heavy Lift Tri-Core, or European Modular Heavy).
  4. Flight Ops: Pilot the exact spacecraft designed in the CAD Bay inside a live 3D WebGL orbital arena (WASD steering, boost, sensor scan pulse, Chase/Cockpit/Overview cameras, and 1x–25x time warp) while monitoring real-time EPS, propellant, and GNC telemetry graphs.
  5. Science: Trigger instrument sweeps into a solid-state flight recorder and downlink data to Earth through a simulated Deep Space Network complex (Goldstone DSS-14 70m) with realistic carrier link margins and light-time delays.
  6. Debrief: Receive a Post-Flight Engineering Review scoring science yield, systems margin, and cost stewardship, with tailored engineering recommendations.

Benefits:

  • Turns abstract aerospace concepts—mass fractions,
    budgets, inverse-square solar decay, eclipse battery sizing, and telecom latency—into immediate visual cause and effect.
  • Requires zero downloads, paid licenses, or specialized hardware, and runs directly in any web browser, including on school devices.
  • Connects every design decision end-to-end: the spacecraft configured in Phase 02 is the exact vehicle launched in Phase 03 and piloted in Phase 04.

Intended impact:
Our goal is to make end-to-end spacecraft systems engineering approachable and hands-on for high school and university STEM students, classrooms, and citizen scientists. By letting learners experiment with competing demands—payload capability vs. propellant mass, solar arrays vs. nuclear MMRTGs, and science yield vs. grant caps—ASTRAEA builds practical engineering intuition for how real space missions are planned and operated.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used:

  • Languages & Core Stack: TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, HTML5/CSS3.
  • 3D Rendering & Audio: WebGL and Three.js for the interactive 3D spacecraft CAD assembly, exploded inspection, and 3D orbital flight simulator, plus the Web Audio API for procedural audio cues.
  • Build & Hosting: Node.js, Vite, and Google Cloud Run for public browser deployment.
  • Presentation & Pitch Export: pptxgenjs and qrcode. React for the interactive 7-slide pitch deck and .pptx export.
  • Hardware: Built and tested on standard consumer laptops, so the simulator runs smoothly without a dedicated GPU.

How it is creative:
Most existing tools either oversimplify space into arcade games with unlimited fuel and power, or hide mission design inside complex, expensive engineering spreadsheets. ASTRAEA unifies concurrent spacecraft CAD assembly, real-time physics margin telemetry, 3D orbital piloting, and Deep Space Network science operations into one continuous interactive game—complete with a Custom Mission Builder so educators and students can design missions to any world they imagine.

Factors considered:

  • Coupled Physics & Competing Demands: Balancing Tsiolkovsky
    against dry payload mass, launch vehicle capacity, and grant limits.
  • Space Environment Extremes: Modeling inverse-square solar irradiance (
    ) from ( near the Sun) to ( at Europa) and ( at Titan), alongside planetary umbra eclipses, radiation tiers, and Stefan-Boltzmann thermal limits.
  • Communications & Latency: Incorporating realistic one-way light-time delays (
    in LEO, at Mars, at Titan) and DSN carrier link margins.
  • Accessibility & Onboarding: Providing a built-in Reference Guide, live nominal/caution telemetry alerts, and a quick-launch 3D flight option alongside the full 6-phase engineering workflow.
